Problem: A reflection takes $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ to $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}.$  Which vector does the reflection take $\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$ to?

Solve step by step. End with: The answer is [your answer].

message.content:
A reflection across a line through the origin has matrix form

\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}
a & b\\
b & -a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad a^2+b^2=1.
\]

It maps \(\begin{pmatrix}5\\0\end{pmatrix}\) to \(\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}\), so

\[
R\begin{pmatrix}5\\0\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}5a\\5b\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Thus

\[
a=\frac45,\qquad b=\frac35.
\]

So

\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}
\frac45 & \frac35\\
\frac35 & -\frac45
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Now apply \(R\) to \(\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}\):

\[
R\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac45(-2)+\frac35(3)\\[2mm]
\frac35(-2)-\frac45(3)
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
-\frac85+\frac95\\[2mm]
-\frac65-\frac{12}{5}
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac15\\[2mm]
-\frac{18}{5}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix}\frac15\\[2mm]-\frac{18}{5}\end{pmatrix}\).
